title: Anchoring Motion, Refining Trajectories: Generalizable Continuous Neural Decoding
abstract: arXiv:2611.21335v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Brain activity encodes motor information across multiple temporal scales, enabling continuous neural control beyond discrete action recognition. However, existing methods are typically tailored to specific subjects and tasks, with direct neural-to-kinematic mappings that can entangle subject-specific neural variability with task-dependent motion patterns, limiting generalization. To address these limitations, we introduce AMRT, a shared neural decoding framework for heterogeneous electrode configurations and movement paradigms. Motivated by cortical encoding of movement direction and speed, AMRT adopts a two-stage design that anchors local motion through velocity estimation and refines the resulting trajectories over longer horizons, encouraging reuse of local motion tendencies across subjects and tasks. translated_title: 锚定运动，精化轨迹：可泛化的连续神经解码
translated_abstract: 脑活动在多个时间尺度上编码运动信息，使连续神经控制超越离散动作识别成为可能。然而，现有方法通常针对特定受试者和任务定制，其直接的神经到运动学映射容易将受试者特异的神经变异性与任务相关的运动模式纠缠在一起，从而限制了泛化能力。为解决这些局限，我们提出了AMRT，一个面向异构电极配置和运动范式的共享神经解码框架。受皮层对运动方向和速度编码机制的启发，AMRT采用两阶段设计：先通过速度估计锚定局部运动，再在更长的时间范围内精化由此得到的轨迹，从而促进局部运动倾向在不同受试者和任务间的复用。在三个数据集上的实验表明，AMRT能够泛化到未见过的试验和受试者，并展现出跨神经记录数据的迁移潜力。
tldr: 提出AMRT共享神经解码框架，通过“速度估计锚定局部运动、长时程精化轨迹”的两阶段设计，实现跨受试者、跨任务和跨电极配置的可泛化连续神经运动解码。
en_tdlr: AMRT is a shared neural decoding framework with a two-stage design—anchoring local motion via velocity estimation and refining trajectories over longer horizons—that enables generalizable continuous neural decoding across unseen subjects, tasks, and heterogeneous electrode configurations.
